picks.title: Eminently controllable, accessible by design, Sting is now a plug-in - CDM Create Digital Music
picks.excerpt: Now this is how to do generative melodies. Add expression. Get control with your hands. Make melodies accessible -- including if you're blind and visually impaired. Sting, the beloved maker of acid melodies and other patterns, is confined to Max for Live no more: now, it's available as VST3, AU, CLAP / macOS, Windows, Linux.
picks.rationale: Generative melody engine escapes Max for Live into VST3/AU/CLAP on every OS — a hands-on tool a producer can load into their DAW tomorrow, with accessibility built in.

picks.title: sonible smart:chain - Can AI Actually Mix Your Song?
picks.rationale: A real test-drive of sonible's AI mix chain rather than a press release — tells you where the automated chain holds up and where you still have to intervene.

picks.title: Sentient, an AUv3 Synthesizer for iOS and macOS powered by a neural network
picks.excerpt: Sentient is an AUv3 Synthesizer for iOS/macOS, powered by a neural network that listens to everyday sounds to build a personalized wavetable
picks.rationale: A neural net that turns recorded everyday sound into personal wavetables — novel sound-design method, and it runs as an AUv3 on hardware people already carry.

picks.title: Denon's Prime 4 G2 is an expressive DJ setup that borrows a few tricks from Akai's MPC range
picks.excerpt: The updated all-in-one DJ system comes equipped with the MPC's multi-touch MPCe pads as well as onboard stem separation
picks.rationale: Standalone hardware with on-device stem separation plus MPC pads — AI source separation moving off the laptop and into the booth changes how a set gets built.

picks.title: Apple's 'Audio Intelligence' includes Shazam music recognition
picks.excerpt: Apple held its latest new-products event last night, with new iPhones (including one that folds), AirPods and Apple Watches. But the most relevant announcement for us was 'Audio Intelligence'.
picks.rationale: The one platform-level story left standing: Apple folds Shazam recognition into an always-on audio layer, which reshapes how listeners discover and credit tracks.
